newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian banks lend less but better - supervisor.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian banks lend less but better - supervisor.

text.p: Lending by Hungarian banks slackened in real terms from 1995 to 1996, although the quality of their loans improved, the State Banking Supervision (BAF) said on Monday, quoted by the Hungarian MTI news agency.

The BAF said in its report on 1995/1996 that the loan portfolio of Hungary's commercial banks totalled 3,119.1 billion forints at the end of June, up 19 percent from 2,623.6 billion forints in the previous year.
June's year-on-year inflation figure was 23.6 percent.
The BAF added that commercial banks' bad loans totalled 111.4 billion forints at the end of June 1996, down from 169 billion forints one year before.
Further loans totalling 287.2 billion forints were categorised as "problematic" as of June 30, compared with 323.6 billion forints' worth at the end of June 1995.
Hungary's government spent more than 300 billion forints on consolidation of the banking system between 1991 and 1994, to help the banks write off bad loans and improve their capital adequacy ratios.
